findings.quote: Such a seed is dormant, so its metabolism is very slow but not zero.
findings.problem: The claim that metabolism cannot be zero is false. Sufficiently dried viable seeds can enter reversible metabolic arrest. They resume metabolism after rehydration. Continuous metabolic activity is not required for a dry seed to remain viable.
findings.source: [Water content, adenylate kinase, and mitochondria drive adenylate balance in dehydrating and imbibing seeds, Journal of Experimental Botany (2017)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5853452/), abstract and introduction.

findings.quote: Cells alone are not enough either: a dead leaf or a piece of wood is made of cells, or what is left of them, but shows none of the other properties.
findings.problem: Wood does not necessarily lack life processes. Sapwood contains living parenchyma cells that carry out metabolism, store and transport nutrients, and respond to damage. A piece of fresh sapwood can contain these active cells. The statement incorrectly treats all wood as dead.
findings.source: [Schenk, Wood: Biology of a living tissue, American Journal of Botany (2018)](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ajb2.1039).
